overview: The Republican Party of Texas platform says the party works to preserve the freedom it describes as given by God, established by the nation's founders, and embodied in the U.S. Constitution. Its preamble names the traditional family, the protection of innocent life, free-market principles, and state and national sovereignty as core commitments.

The document is titled the 2026 Platform and Resolutions of the Republican Party of Texas and was posted by the party as the approved 2026 platform. It opens with ten numbered principles, followed by 285 numbered planks in sections such as Constitutional Issues, Finance, Education, and Border Security and Immigration, and ends with four resolutions.

values.text: The party says its principles rest on belief in God and calls for following the original language and intent of the Declaration of Independence and the U.S. and Texas Constitutions.
values.quote: we recognize the historic and continuing influence of Christianity in securing our rights and liberties as endowed by our Creator

values.text: The party says human life should be protected by law from fertilization until natural death.
values.quote: The sanctity of innocent human life, created in the image of God, which should be equally protected from fertilization to natural death.

values.text: The party says government power should be limited to what the U.S. and Texas Constitutions list, and that individual, Texan, and American sovereignty should be preserved.
values.quote: Limiting government power to those items enumerated in the United States and Texas Constitutions.

values.text: The party says families should be self-sufficient and founded on marriage between one man and one woman.
values.quote: Self-sufficient families, founded on the traditional marriage of one natural man and one natural woman.

values.text: The party says parents should have full freedom to choose how, where, and by whom their children are educated.
values.quote: Parents having the complete freedom of choice for the education of their children

values.text: The party says people have a permanent right to defend themselves and their property.
values.quote: The right of all people to defend themselves and their property is inalienable.

values.text: The party says the economy should be free of government interference and that economic and property rights should stay in force even during emergencies.
values.quote: economic liberty and private property rights shall not be suspended, even during declared emergencies

areas.Abortion: The platform calls for abolishing abortion by giving legal protection to unborn children from fertilization (Planks 23 and 218). Until then, it supports restrictions such as parental consent, bans after a heartbeat is detected, a ban on abortion pills, and limits on help with travel for abortions, while keeping the current medical emergency exceptions (Planks 160 and 216).
areas.County Government: The platform calls for 12-year term limits for state and county offices and for limiting local government spending growth to the lesser of population growth plus inflation or 3.5 percent unless voters approve more (Planks 2 and 66). It also supports giving county commissioners courts limited authority to regulate large commercial projects, such as solar farms and data centers, in unincorporated areas (Plank 221).
areas.Courts: The platform calls for strict construction of the U.S. and Texas Constitutions, opposes enlarging the U.S. Supreme Court, and supports letting Congress limit the Supreme Court's jurisdiction (Planks 1, 6, and 7). It also supports narrowing judicial, prosecutorial, and qualified immunity, informing jurors of their power to judge the law, a process for the Attorney General to remove district attorneys who do not enforce state law, and bail based on danger, flight risk, and criminal history (Planks 169, 178, 179, and 182).
areas.Education: The platform supports school choice with funding that follows the student, full funding of Texas Education Freedom Accounts, and abolishing the U.S. Department of Education (Planks 89 and 108). It calls for ending sex education in public schools, replacing the STAAR test, and spending at least 80 percent of district revenue on classroom instruction (Planks 81, 94, and 103).
areas.Elections and Ethics: The platform calls for photo ID for all methods of voting, paper ballots, an early voting period of no more than three days, a ban on ranked choice voting, closed party primaries, and repeal of motor voter laws (Planks 250, 251, 252, and 255). It also calls for repealing limits on campaign contributions by American citizens, abolishing the Texas Ethics Commission, and banning taxpayer-funded lobbying (Planks 227, 239, and 246).
areas.Energy and Environment: The platform supports free-market energy policy without subsidies or mandates, development of all energy sources, next-generation nuclear power, and keeping the Texas grid independent (Planks 45, 51, and 52). It calls for abolishing the Environmental Protection Agency, repealing the Endangered Species Act, and classifying carbon dioxide as a non-pollutant, and says data centers should pay for the water and power infrastructure they need (Planks 43, 46, and 50).
areas.Family and Social Policy: The platform defines marriage as between one man and one woman, says the Obergefell same-sex marriage ruling should be nullified, and calls for ending unilateral no-fault divorce (Planks 207, 209, and 211). It also supports a parental rights amendment to the Texas Constitution, opposes gender transition treatment for minors, and opposes expanding gambling (Planks 18, 69, and 148).
areas.Guns and Public Safety: The platform calls for unrestricted constitutional carry, repeal of the National Firearms Act and Gun Control Act, no gun-free zones, and letting license holders carry on school campuses (Planks 2, 20, 112, and 230). It supports capital punishment, keeps marijuana illegal, and calls for maximum penalties for illegal drug makers and distributors (Planks 151, 188, and 229).
areas.Health Care: The platform calls for repealing the Affordable Care Act and replacing it with free-market legislation that keeps protections for preexisting conditions, and it opposes expanding Medicaid (Planks 141 and 143). It supports a state health savings account to help Texas leave the federal Medicaid program, higher contribution limits for individual health savings accounts, and a constitutional right to refuse vaccines and other medical treatment (Planks 130, 135, and 136).
areas.Immigration and Border: The platform calls for funding a border wall and barriers, a state Border Protection Unit, devoting all available resources to deportations, and opposing amnesty in all forms (Planks 263, 264, 267, and 268). It also supports mandatory E-Verify for employers, requiring all Texas law enforcement agencies to cooperate with federal immigration enforcement, and a pause on net migration (Planks 266, 270, and 271).
areas.Jobs and Wages: The platform calls for repealing federal minimum wage and prevailing wage laws, ending required sick and family leave, and eliminating business and professional licensing (Planks 26 and 28). It supports a national right-to-work law, ending special collective bargaining laws for public employees, and privatizing Social Security (Planks 38, 39, and 42).
areas.Land and Agriculture: The platform says eminent domain should be limited to clear public necessity and never used for private economic development, and it calls for limiting land ownership in Texas to U.S. citizens and U.S. companies, with an exception for lawful immigrants (Planks 224 and 226). It supports tying groundwater rights to surface ownership, letting people buy farm products directly from farmers, and a right to repair farm equipment (Planks 28, 32, and 50).
areas.Taxes and Spending: The platform calls for eliminating property taxes, using 90 percent or more of any state budget surplus to buy down school property taxes, and setting strict spending limits on state and local governments (Planks 66, 79, and 80). It also supports repealing the federal income tax, abolishing inventory and business franchise taxes, and ending tax breaks and subsidies for favored businesses (Planks 72, 73, and 83).

republican.notes: Read from the official PDF (59 pages). Plank numbers and page numbers refer to that document. The document does not state the date or city of the convention that approved it; the guide.json summary (June 2026, Houston) could not be confirmed from the document itself.

overview: The Texas Democratic Party platform describes itself as a statement of broad ideals shared by Democrats across Texas, built on what it calls the values of family, privacy, freedom, and fairness. It says a well-functioning government acts for the benefit of the people and of the many, relies on facts and evidence, and should provide a social safety net.

The platform covers 2026 to 2028 and states that it was passed at the 2026 Texas Democratic Convention in Corpus Christi in June 2026. It is organized into 21 sections, from Affordability and Healthcare to Immigration and Foreign Policy, and closes with a Principles and Beliefs section.

values.text: The party says government should work for the benefit of most people rather than a few.
values.quote: A well-functioning government acts for the benefit of the many, not the few.

values.text: The party lists rights it says belong to every Texan, including voting, public education, affordable health care, due process, a clean planet, and privacy.
values.quote: Every Texan has inalienable rights that even a majority may not take away

values.text: The party says government should stay out of people's private lives and personal decisions.
values.quote: Limited government interference in our private lives and personal decisions

values.text: The party says people are responsible for their actions and should give back to their communities.
values.quote: That people are responsible for their actions

values.text: The party says every person is entitled to equal protection and due process under the law.
values.quote: No state may deny any person equal protection of the laws or due process under the law

values.text: The party says economic growth should benefit all Texans, workers should earn a living wage, and taxes should be fairly shared.
values.quote: That every person should be paid a living wage

values.text: The party says the contributions of different people and groups make Texas stronger.
values.quote: Texas is made stronger by the collective strengths and contributions of diverse individuals, groups, and populations

areas.Abortion: The platform calls for repealing Texas's abortion ban, the Texas Heartbeat Act, and limits on medication abortion, and for protecting access to contraception and IVF (Healthcare, page 11). It also calls for repealing laws that make abortion care, miscarriage, or reproductive health decisions a crime (Criminal Justice Reform, page 40).
areas.County Government: The platform calls for giving counties more development authority outside city limits, ending unfunded state mandates that it says drive up county property tax rates, and letting counties and cities regulate large data centers (Affordability, pages 4 to 5; Rural Texas, page 25). It also supports a recall process for state and county officials and public defender offices or assigned counsel programs in all 254 counties (Democracy, page 29; Criminal Justice Reform, page 41).
areas.Courts: The platform supports 18-year term limits and staggered appointments for federal judges, including U.S. Supreme Court justices, a binding ethics code for federal judges, and keeping elections for Texas judges (Democracy, pages 32 to 33). It also calls for ending cash bail practices that jail people only because they cannot pay and for eliminating mandatory minimum sentences for nonviolent offenses (Criminal Justice Reform, pages 41 to 43).
areas.Education: The platform calls for fully funding public schools, universal pre-K, higher teacher pay, and replacing high-stakes testing with multiple measures of student growth (Education, pages 13 to 15). It calls for repealing the Texas school voucher program, opposes expanding charter schools without accountability, and supports tuition-free community college (Education, pages 13 and 16).
areas.Elections and Ethics: The platform calls for automatic or same-day voter registration, longer early voting, universal vote by mail, repeal of the Texas photo voter ID law, a citizen-led redistricting commission, and ranked-choice voting (Democracy, pages 32 to 33). It also supports overturning the Citizens United decision, public financing of campaigns, and banning stock trading by elected officials (Democracy, pages 29 to 34).
areas.Energy and Environment: The platform calls for a statewide climate action plan, growth of clean energy, retiring coal power as quickly as possible, and stricter enforcement of methane and air pollution rules (Energy and The Environment, pages 17 to 19). It also supports reforming the Texas Railroad Commission and the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality, weatherizing the power grid, and treating clean air and water as a basic right (pages 18 to 21).
areas.Family and Social Policy: The platform supports paid sick, vacation, and family leave, affordable child care, and a minimum marriage age of 18 (Good Jobs, page 7; Quality of Life, page 35). It also supports marriage equality and nondiscrimination protections for LGBTQIA+ Texans, adoption and foster care without discriminatory barriers, and a universal basic income (Equality and Social Justice, page 49; Quality of Life, pages 35 to 36).
areas.Guns and Public Safety: The platform says it seeks to preserve Second Amendment rights while requiring universal background checks, waiting periods, safe storage, and limits on large-capacity magazines, and it supports letting voters decide on raising the purchase age for semiautomatic rifles to 21 (Public Safety, page 38). It also calls for police body cameras, legalizing cannabis for adults, and treating drug use and mental health as public health issues (Criminal Justice Reform, pages 40 to 43).
areas.Health Care: The platform says health care should be a basic right and calls for expanding Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act and moving toward a universal health care system that includes a public option (Healthcare, page 10). It also supports lowering prescription drug prices and capping insulin costs at $35 per month (Healthcare, page 10).
areas.Immigration and Border: The platform calls for comprehensive immigration reform, including a path to legal status for undocumented immigrants who pass a background check and a path to citizenship (Immigration, page 55). It supports securing the border with technology, ending Operation Lone Star and family detention, restoring in-state tuition for undocumented students, and keeping local police independent from federal immigration enforcement (Immigration, pages 55 to 57).
areas.Jobs and Wages: The platform supports a living wage tied to inflation, letting cities and counties set wages above the state minimum, and equal pay for equal work (Good Jobs and Workers' Rights, page 6). It calls for repealing right-to-work laws, protecting the right to join a union and bargain collectively, and promoting a 32-hour work week without loss of pay (pages 6 to 7).
areas.Land and Agriculture: The platform calls for breaking up monopolies in farm supplies and food processing, a right to repair farm equipment, and fair prices for producers (Consumer Protection, page 9; Texas Agriculture, page 22). It also supports reforming eminent domain laws, protecting farmers' groundwater from large corporate users and data centers, and country-of-origin labels on food (Texas Agriculture, pages 22 to 23).
areas.Taxes and Spending: The platform calls for raising taxes on billionaires, expanding the Earned Income Tax Credit, making the Child Tax Credit fully refundable, and letting voters adopt a flat-dollar homestead exemption (Affordability, page 4). It also supports temporarily freezing residential property appraisals, taxing commercial and industrial property at market value, reducing tax incentives for businesses that shift tax burdens onto residents, and using the Rainy Day Fund during downturns and disasters (Affordability, pages 4 to 5).

democratic.notes: Read from the official PDF (68 pages including committee roster). Page numbers are the printed page numbers at the bottom of each page. The cover states the platform was passed at the convention in Corpus Christi in June 2026, but the exact day is left blank in the document.

overview: The Libertarian Party of Texas (LPTexas) platform says the party seeks a world in which all individuals are sovereign over their lives, and it opposes the use of force, coercion, or fraud to reach personal, political, or social goals. It holds that government should exist only to defend individual freedoms and should be kept to the minimum needed to protect individual rights.

The platform is labeled as amended at the 2026 State Convention and revised April 12, 2026. It is organized into sections on Personal Liberty, Economic Liberty, and Liberty to Immigrate and Freely Trade, plus several other planks, and its Omissions section says silence on any issue should not be read as approval, disapproval, or indifference.

values.text: The party says all human interaction should be voluntary, and that no one should start the use of force or fraud against others.
values.quote: LPTexas holds that all human interaction should be voluntary and consensual, in accordance with the Non-Aggression Principle.

values.text: The party says each person owns their own body and mind and should be free to live as they choose.
values.quote: Every human being is born sole owner of body and mind, free to live and act as each individual sees fit.

values.text: The party says the only proper role of government is to protect people's freedoms.
values.quote: Governments may only exist for the sole purpose of defending the freedoms of people.

values.text: The party says people should be free to do anything that is peaceful and honest.
values.quote: we defend each person’s right to engage in any activity that is peaceful and honest.

values.text: The party says everyone should be treated equally under the law and be free to trade with one another in a free market.
values.quote: All people should be equal before the law, free to deal with one another in a free market

values.text: The party says government should rest on the consent of the people and should not let a majority override individual rights.
values.quote: Government should reflect the consent of the governed and not subject individuals to tyranny of the majority.

values.text: The party says people have an inherent right to own property, including land, belongings, and their own bodies.
values.quote: Property rights are subject to neither infringement nor interference by any individual or governmental entity.

areas.Abortion: The platform says reproductive rights are a sensitive issue on which people hold good-faith views, and that government should stay out of the matter and leave the decision to each person (Section I.3.e). It also says tax dollars should not pay for such medical costs (Section I.3.e).
areas.County Government: The platform does not address this area directly.
areas.Courts: The platform supports informing jurors of possible sentences and of their right to judge the law itself, known as jury nullification, and calls for abolishing legal doctrines such as qualified immunity that shield government employees from liability (Sections I.6.a and I.6.d). It opposes the death penalty and says property should be forfeited only after a criminal conviction (Sections I.2.b, I.2.c, and I.6.c).
areas.Education: The platform calls for eliminating truancy laws and other barriers to school choice and says parents and guardians should decide where and how their children are educated (Section II.2.a). It rejects any federal involvement in local schools, including funding, and sets a long-term goal of voluntary education funding (Section II.2.a).
areas.Elections and Ethics: The platform supports verifiable ballot receipts or electronic tracking, a None of The Above option in all elections, and transparency in candidate and campaign funding (Sections I.5.a and I.5.d). It opposes party labels on the ballot and straight-ticket voting, and says each party should choose and pay for its own candidate selection under its own rules (Sections I.5.b and I.5.d).
areas.Energy and Environment: The platform supports an energy future led by voluntary markets rather than political mandates, including oil, gas, wind, solar, and modern nuclear power (Section II.4). It calls for rolling back regulations that block energy innovation while keeping protections for human safety, property rights, and imminent threats to the environment, and for opening the grid to competition (Section II.4).
areas.Family and Social Policy: The platform says relationships between consenting adults are a private matter that the state should not define, license, or restrict, and it seeks to abolish laws that define what a family is (Sections I.1.d and I.1.e). It says helping people in need is the role of communities and charities, and calls for phasing out taxpayer-funded welfare programs once private alternatives are free to operate (Section I.4.b).
areas.Guns and Public Safety: The platform supports the right to buy, make, own, and carry arms, including body armor, for defense of person and property (Section I.1.b). It opposes the War on Drugs, calls for repealing vice and morality laws that apply to consenting adults who do no harm to others, and supports limiting no-knock warrants (Sections I.3.c, I.4.c, and I.6.b).
areas.Health Care: The platform says health care decisions should be personal and voluntary, and it opposes taxpayer-funded health care systems and government mandates to wear protective equipment or receive medical treatment (Sections I.3.b and I.3.f). It calls for removing legal barriers to private, charitable, and community-based health care options and supports the right to end one's life with dignity (Sections I.3.b and I.3.d).
areas.Immigration and Border: The platform supports the freedom of individuals to live, work, study, and travel without government barriers, with respect for the rights of others (Section III). It also supports the free and voluntary exchange of goods, labor, services, and ideas (Section III).
areas.Jobs and Wages: The platform says working in an occupation is a natural right and calls for repealing all occupational licensing laws, with any government role limited to protecting against fraud or abuse (Section II.1.a). It supports the voluntary exchange of labor and services and does not address minimum wage laws directly (Section III).
areas.Land and Agriculture: The platform opposes the use of eminent domain in any form and calls for abolishing civil asset forfeiture (Sections I.2.a and I.2.b). It also opposes requirements to register property with the government except to document clear title, and it does not address agriculture directly (Section I.4.a).
areas.Taxes and Spending: The platform says every tax is theft and calls for ending all taxation, with any remaining taxes minimized or replaced by user fees (Section II.1). It also supports a halt to government borrowing, including bonds and certificates of obligation, and selling government-owned assets to pay off existing debt (Section II.1.b).

libertarian.notes: Read from the official PDF dated April 12, 2026. Section numbers follow the platform's own numbering; page numbers are the printed 'of 13' page numbers. The document does not mention county government. It does not state the city of the 2026 State Convention.

overview: The Green Party of Texas platform says it expresses the party's commitment to meaningful and enduring change in the political process, and it describes the party as an alternative to what it calls the corporately controlled political system. It says its positions stem from the Ten Key Values of the Green Party, including grassroots democracy, social justice, ecological wisdom, nonviolence, and decentralization.

The platform is titled the Green Party of Texas State Platform (2021) and is posted with a note that it is up to date as of December 2023. It describes itself as a living document drafted, amended, and adopted by the party membership through an open process, and it is organized into five sections: Grassroots Democracy, Social Justice and Equal Opportunity, Ecological Sustainability, Economic Sustainability, and Non-violence.

values.text: The party says all people should take part directly in the decisions that affect their lives.
values.quote: We believe in direct participation by all people in the environmental, political, and economic decisions that affect their lives.

values.text: The party says human well-being depends on the natural world and that harm to nature, animals, and people share common roots.
values.quote: We recognize that the Earth sustains all life processes.

values.text: The party says it seeks to end poverty and oppression based on class, sex, race, citizenship, age, or sexual orientation.
values.quote: We want to replace the worldwide system of poverty and injustice with a world free of all oppression based on class, sex, race, citizenship, age, or sexual orientation.

values.text: The party says it rejects violence as a way to settle disputes and works toward a world without war.
values.quote: We work to create a world where war is obsolete.

values.text: The party says power and responsibility should be returned to local communities.
values.quote: Power and responsibility must be restored to local communities

values.text: The party says the economy should meet everyone's basic needs within the Earth's natural limits and under local, democratic control.
values.quote: We seek a new economics based upon the natural limits of the Earth which meets the basic needs of everyone on the planet

values.text: The party says decisions should give the interests of future generations equal weight with those of people living today.
values.quote: we seek a society where the interests of the seventh generation yet to come are considered equal to the interests of the present generation

areas.Abortion: The platform supports the right of women to make their own decisions about all aspects of reproduction without government restriction, and it supports publicly funded, medically accurate sex education and family planning as a way to reduce the need for abortion (Section II.A). It also opposes coerced abortion, sterilization, or contraception (Section II.A).
areas.County Government: The platform calls for barring county office candidates from accepting donations from outside their counties and for independent civilian review boards with subpoena power at the city and county levels to oversee police misconduct cases (Sections I.A and II.C). In counties of fewer than 35,000 people, it supports requiring national chains to win a public referendum before getting business or building permits, and it calls for city and county input on new toll roads (Sections III.C and IV.C).
areas.Courts: The platform calls for abolishing the death penalty, trying juvenile offenders as juveniles, repealing mandatory sentencing laws such as three strikes, and setting uniform standards and public hearings for clemency (Section II.C). It also supports ending qualified immunity for police, independent prosecution of officers accused of misconduct, and grand jury reform (Section II.C).
areas.Education: The platform opposes school vouchers, calls for equitable state funding for all public schools, and opposes relying mainly on high-stakes standardized tests for promotion, graduation, or teacher pay (Section II.H). It supports teacher salaries comparable to similar professions, the right of teacher unions to strike, expanded bilingual education, and free tuition at Texas public colleges for Texas high school graduates (Section II.H).
areas.Elections and Ethics: The platform calls for full public financing of election campaigns, preferential voting methods such as approval voting, proportional representation, same-day and online voter registration, a binding none of the above option, and an end to gerrymandering (Sections I.A and I.B). It also supports hand-counted paper ballots, a citizen right of initiative and referendum, a ban on gifts from lobbyists to officials, and a ban on corporate contributions to political parties (Sections I.A and I.B).
areas.Energy and Environment: The platform calls for a state energy plan overseen by an elected energy commission, making renewable energy a priority, a planned phase-out of coal and petroleum, a ban on coal mining in Texas, and retiring the state's nuclear power reactors (Section III.F). It also calls for stronger clean air and water enforcement, capping abandoned oil and gas wells, and recycling services for all homes and businesses (Sections III.A, III.B, and III.G).
areas.Family and Social Policy: The platform supports legal recognition of same-sex civil marriage and protection for gay, lesbian, bisexual, and transgender people from discrimination in housing, jobs, child custody, and adoption (Section II.B). It also opposes corporal punishment of children, supports lowering the voting age to 16, and says government should play an active role in providing affordable housing (Sections II.B and II.E).
areas.Guns and Public Safety: The platform says the party does not oppose lawful gun ownership and supports background checks on all secondary gun sales, licensing and registration of newly bought handguns and assault weapons, a limit of one handgun purchase per month, and a required gun safety course (Section II.G). On policing, it supports body cameras that officers cannot turn off, demilitarizing police, shifting funds from policing and prisons to mental health and social services, and decriminalizing marijuana (Sections II.C and II.D).
areas.Health Care: The platform endorses a universal single-payer health care system, in which one public program pays for care, and says health care is a human right that should not depend on income, employment, health status, or place of birth (Section II.A). Until then, it calls for more funding for the Children's Health Insurance Program and expanding it to cover adult parents, and it supports access to medical cannabis (Section II.A).
areas.Immigration and Border: The platform calls for a comprehensive legalization program for all undocumented people living in the United States, a path to permanent residency and citizenship for immigrant workers, and an end to the militarization of the border with Mexico (Section II.I). It also says immigrants should have the same labor and civil rights as citizens and calls for removing limits on their access to legal and social service programs (Section II.I).
areas.Jobs and Wages: The platform supports a living wage high enough for a minimum-wage worker to afford a one-bedroom apartment where they work, along with a guaranteed minimum income or basic income for all (Sections IV.B and IV.G). It supports collective bargaining rights for any two or more workers, protection from firing without just cause, overtime pay after 40 hours, a long-term goal of a 32-hour work week with no loss of pay, and support for small businesses and cooperatives (Sections IV.A and IV.G).
areas.Land and Agriculture: The platform supports a shift from corporate agribusiness to sustainable farming, family-owned farms and ranches, an end to factory farming, and labeling of genetically engineered food along with a pause on such products (Sections III.D and III.E). It calls for ending the rule of capture for groundwater, keeping public lands in public hands, and curbing urban sprawl through measures such as urban growth boundaries (Sections III.B and III.H).
areas.Taxes and Spending: The platform supports a progressive tax system based on all income and calls for replacing the state sales tax with a graduated income tax, creating a corporate income tax in Texas, and raising corporate taxes (Section II.F). It also calls for ending tax subsidies and loopholes that favor powerful interests, eliminating the state lottery, taxing industrial pollution, and charging impact fees on new developments (Section II.F).

green.notes: The text was read from Internet Archive snapshots of txgreens.org: the platform page dated October 17, 2026, and the Ten Key Values page dated September 22, 2026, because the live site returned a bot check. The platform is titled the Green Party of Texas State Platform (2021) and is marked as up to date as of December 2023. The web page has no page numbers, so section references follow the platform's own numbering.
